A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VGR and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The complete 18-page v1 and 23-page v3 support comparison. Reporting inconsistencies in some tables affect their interpretation, not material availability.

before.justification: v1 reports original VGR benchmark evaluations, component and data ablations, token-scaling experiments, and additional backbone experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds high-resolution and grounding evaluations, transfer experiments, robustness analyses, and inference-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The core feature-replay mechanism, pooling, losses, and data-curation pipeline are retained; renaming them around visual memory does not establish a redesign. Appendix B.4 adds a limited procedural adaptation: VGR-style post-training of pretrained InternVL3-8B without the full pretraining-plus-SFT pipeline.

E1.justification: v3 adds dedicated high-resolution evaluations on V* Bench and HR-Bench 8K, plus referring-expression comprehension on RefCOCO, RefCOCOg, and RefCOCO+ (Tables 3 and 13). These substantially extend evaluation populations and task requirements. The original training-data sources and benchmark coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the original benchmark and CoT-data comparisons remain unchanged. v3 additionally evaluates LLaVA-NeXT with ZoomEye against VGR (Table 10), and introduces matched non-VGR controls for the Qwen2.5-based configurations and InternVL3 post-training experiments (Tables 3 and 14).

E3.justification: New experimental designs include Qwen2.5-7B with SigLIP or InternViT, an InternVL3-8B post-training comparison, matched 25K annotation-source comparisons, and corrupted-box and absolute-coordinate tests. v3 also introduces REC evaluation using accuracy at IoU greater than 0.5 and IoU, alongside latency and generation-cost measurements. These extend the protocols rather than establish reruns of the retained experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses of cached-memory replay versus re-encoding crops, annotation source and data scale, inaccurate replay boxes, coordinate normalization, architectural transfer, and inference behavior. Figure 6 adds a sequential visual-search case study. Existing component ablations and token-scaling analyses are retained; the random-box analysis is added but its numerical support is internally inconsistent.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The newly reported average latency and cross-benchmark range of valid-box rates are descriptive results, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and ablation scores are retained, while numerous new outcomes are reported. For example, v3 Table 10 reports VGR versus ZoomEye scores of 67.7 versus 71.7 on V* Bench and 52.9 versus 44.4 on HR-Bench, with substantially shorter VGR latency. These are new comparisons, not v1-to-v3 performance gains. Table 12 duplicates Table 9's two 25K-data result rows under different benchmark headings, making its corruption findings unreliable.

T1.justification: v1 Equation 3 explicitly defines feature-region extraction through coordinate-to-index conversion and nearest-integer rounding. v3 omits that mathematical definition and retains only a prose description of extraction. The remaining patch, embedding, and detection-loss equations are unchanged; no theoretical guarantees or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The introduction and contribution list drop explicit first-attempt claims about constructing reasoning data with visual cues, although a related first-time claim remains in the conclusion. The central grounded-reasoning and token-efficiency contributions, including the abstract's reported benchmark improvements, are retained.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of memory reuse versus recropping, increased latency from reasoning and replay, and the limitations of the post-training-only InternVL3 probe. It interprets new experiments as supporting grounding accuracy and transferability, though Table 12 does not reliably support its corruption interpretation. Section 5.4 also emphasizes OCR benefits from unchanged token-scaling results instead of v1's more cautious discussion of dataset-dependent gains.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses one-epoch training, 0.03 warmup, cosine scheduling, zero weight decay, H20 GPUs for timing, and default Doubao settings with an 8192-token response limit. These are disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to existing settings. A new reproducibility statement promises code and checkpoint release; the PDFs do not establish that release occurred. Existing data-access information and detailed annotation prompts are retained.

R1.justification: Related-work coverage expands to ZoomEye, Chain-of-Spot, SketchPad, Refocus, and Chain-of-Focus. New Appendix E substantially develops VGR's positioning against these approaches and previously cited Visual CoT and CogCom, emphasizing flexible replay, precomputed visual memory, and the data-and-training pipeline. This goes beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the abstract and substantial introductory, data-curation, and experimental prose around visual-memory terminology. It reorganizes the ablation narrative, moves v1 Section 5.5 into Appendix D.2, and redistributes existing appendix material across separate sections. Conference statements, author/header edits, and author-year citations accompany this broader restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn as a simpler pipeline, existing training examples are relocated, and the long-versus-short reasoning illustration moves from the main text to the appendix. v3 adds Figure 6 and multiple experimental tables, while the pooling table gains a memory column and comparison row. The conference template also changes headings, captions, and page layout.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the retained work more assessable through targeted high-resolution and grounding evaluations, a qualified transfer probe, actual latency measurements, and additional implementation details. However, new Table 12 repeats unrelated Table 9 results under different headings, and Table 3 appears to swap the retained Vicuna results' AI2D and RWQA columns relative to Table 2. These reporting problems weaken parts of the added evidence and limit the overall benefit.
